intro: Lesson 22: 3.2 Salah: nature, significance and importance. To understand the nature of salah and why it is so important in Muslim life

questions.q: Explain two reasons why salah is important to Muslims. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: It is a pillar commanded by Allah for His remembrance (20:14); it keeps a Muslim from wrongdoing (29:45).
questions.model: Point 1: it is a direct command for remembering Allah. Develop: 'establish prayer for My remembrance' (20:14). Point 2: it protects from sin. Develop: 'prayer prohibits immorality' (29:45), so regular prayer shapes behaviour.

questions.q: How many daily prayers are fard?

In the portal response box: 'Explain how salah affects the life of a Muslim teenager.' Two developed paragraphs (personal discipline; community and character). Start: 'Salah shapes a Muslim teenager's day because ...'
questions.a: Paragraphs on timetable and discipline, avoiding wrong (29:45), equality in the line, khushu'
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'Salah shapes a Muslim teenager's day because the five times (4:103) mean planning homework and sleep around Fajr and Isha.'

questions.q: what does the hadith in Muslim about abandoning prayer show?
questions.a: Salah is the dividing line between belief and disbelief, showing its importance.

questions.q: how is salah different from du'a?
questions.a: Salah is a set ritual with conditions and pillars; du'a is personal asking at any time.

questions.q: Back to our ponder: burden or gift?
questions.a: A gift: a direct meeting with Allah bringing peace and discipline.
